facts.claim: Belief in school meritocracy reduces the perceived unfairness of social class inequality in society.
facts.quote: the belief that schools are meritocratic carries consequences beyond the school context as it is associated with attitudes that maintain social class and economic inequality.

facts.claim: Belief in school meritocracy reduces support for affirmative action policies at university.
facts.quote: belief in school meritocracy reduces the perceived unfairness of social class inequality in society, support for affirmative action policies at university and support for policies aimed at reducing income inequality.

facts.claim: Those with the strongest belief in meritocracy in the creative sector are those in the most privileged positions.
facts.quote: Second, those with the strongest belief in meritocracy in the sector are those in the most privileged positions, specifically those are best rewarded by the sector.

facts.claim: In Indonesia, information describing (high) income inequality and (low) social mobility rocked our participants’ belief in meritocracy.
facts.quote: In Indonesia, information describing (high) income inequality and (low) social mobility rocked our participants’ belief in meritocracy.

facts.claim: Subjective upward mobility is linked to stronger meritocratic beliefs.
facts.quote: subjective upward mobility is associated with stronger meritocratic beliefs, and downward mobility is associated with stronger structuralist beliefs—but has no bearing on people’s meritocracy beliefs.

rejected.claim: In societies where meritocratic perceptions are more prevalent, different social strata are more polarised in their attitudes towards income inequality.
rejected.quote: Our results show that different social strata are indeed more polarised in their attitudes towards inequality in societies where meritocratic perceptions are more prevalent.
rejected.reason: quote not found in the source

research.angle: Belief in meritocracy is linked to the maintenance of social inequality, as it reduces support for redistributive policies and is most strongly held by those in privileged positions.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that meritocratic beliefs are associated with the legitimization of existing social hierarchies and a reduction in support for policies aimed at addressing inequality.
research.caveat: Several key findings are based on observational studies that show associations rather than direct causation.
